questions.stem: A student sets up a respirometer with germinating peas and soda lime (which absorbs CO₂). The coloured liquid in the manometer tube moves towards the peas over 30 minutes. What does this indicate?

options.text: The peas are releasing oxygen during photosynthesis
The peas are absorbing oxygen during respiration, and the CO₂ produced is absorbed by soda lime
The soda lime is releasing gas into the tube
The peas are producing more CO₂ than they are using O₂

questions.explanation: The germinating peas use oxygen for aerobic respiration. The CO₂ they produce is absorbed by soda lime, so the total gas volume in the tube decreases. This causes the liquid to move towards the peas, showing net oxygen uptake.

questions.stem: In a respiration experiment, a student uses hydrogencarbonate indicator solution, which turns yellow in the presence of excess CO₂. A tube containing living woodlice turns yellow after 20 minutes. A control tube with no organisms stays orange-red. What can be concluded?

options.text: The woodlice are carrying out photosynthesis
The indicator changed colour due to temperature changes
The woodlice are producing CO₂ through respiration
The woodlice absorbed oxygen from the indicator solution

questions.explanation: Hydrogencarbonate indicator turns yellow when CO₂ concentration increases (becomes more acidic). The woodlice produce CO₂ as a product of aerobic respiration, causing the colour change. The control confirms the change is due to the organisms, not other factors.

questions.stem: A student wants to compare the respiration rate of germinating seeds at 20°C and 30°C using a respirometer. Which variable must be kept constant to make the comparison valid?

options.text: The temperature of the water bath
The mass and number of germinating seeds used
The colour of the manometer fluid
The species of soda lime used

questions.explanation: To make a fair comparison, control variables must be kept constant. The mass and number of seeds directly affects the amount of respiration occurring, so these must be the same in both setups. Temperature is the independent variable being changed.

questions.stem: A respirometer is set up with boiled (dead) peas as a control alongside living peas. Why is this control important?

options.text: To show that boiled peas respire faster than living peas
To account for any volume changes due to temperature or pressure fluctuations, not respiration
To provide extra CO₂ for the soda lime to absorb
To prove that all seeds can carry out anaerobic respiration

questions.explanation: The boiled peas cannot respire (they are dead). Any movement of the manometer fluid in the control tube must be due to physical changes like temperature or pressure fluctuations. This allows the student to subtract these effects from the living peas' results.

questions.stem: A student places a bell jar over a plant in the dark with hydrogencarbonate indicator. After several hours the indicator has turned yellow. Why did this happen?

options.text: The plant carried out photosynthesis, releasing oxygen
In the dark, the plant only respires, releasing CO₂ which made the indicator more acidic
The indicator naturally turns yellow over time
The plant absorbed all the CO₂, making the solution more alkaline

questions.explanation: In the dark, photosynthesis cannot occur (no light energy), so the plant only carries out respiration. This releases CO₂, which dissolves in the indicator solution making it more acidic and turning it yellow.
